office_does: The prosecuting attorney decides which crimes are charged and prosecutes them, and is the legal adviser and civil lawyer for county officials.
race_blurb: Greg Banks, prosecutor since 1999 and running with no party preference, faces Andrew Scott (Prefers Democratic Party), a former Missoula chief city prosecutor who reached the ballot as a primary write-in. The race turns on Banks's prosecution of a former county Republican chair and on how charges are filed and later escalated.

candidates.summary: Freeland attorney and former chief prosecuting attorney for the City of Missoula, Montana, who reached the ballot with 1,437 primary write-in votes; has not held elected office.
highlights: Published a 'Complete Initial Charging' policy against filing a misdemeanor and later refiling as a felony when plea talks fail [S3]
Wants faster charging decisions, more victim communication and closer coordination with the sheriff [S1][S5]
Would add mental-health and other treatment courts alongside the existing drug court [S5]
Would prioritize serious and repeat offenses [S3]
About 16 years as a Missoula city prosecutor, mostly misdemeanors, rising to chief [S1][S5]

safety.basis: Leans to treatment courts and limits on overcharging and charge escalation, while also pledging to prioritize serious and repeat offenses and work with law enforcement.

experience.basis: Never elected and challenging a 28-year incumbent as the change candidate, though he has about 16 years of city prosecution behind him.

candidates.summary: Island County Prosecuting Attorney since 1999, seeking an eighth term with no party preference; vice president of the National District Attorneys Association and endorsed by Gov. Ferguson, AG Nick Brown and former AG Rob McKenna.
highlights: Cites 'successfully prosecuting serious offenses and standing up for crime victims' [S1]
Personally prosecuted former county GOP chair Tim Hazelo, convicted by a jury in 2025 [S14]
Won a unanimous state Supreme Court case against the commissioners' hiring of outside lawyers [S3]
Says he and his deputies trained all Oak Harbor and county officers in 2026 [S3]
A visiting judge disqualified his office from a related public-records suit in August 2026 [S13]

safety.basis: Stresses prosecuting serious offenses, victims' rights and officer training, mentioning drug courts and alternative sentencing only in general terms.

experience.basis: 28-year incumbent with seven election wins, a felony and Supreme Court record, and state and national prosecutor-association leadership.
